# Make

The old dependency-graph task runner, used here purely as a **named-command registry** rather than
for incremental rebuilds. [[labour-fraud-analysis]] carries the only Makefile across the repositories
ingested with it; [[data-warehousing-and-business-intelligence]] has no build entry point at all.

Thirteen phony targets: `all`, `data`, `db`, `docs`, `report`, `viewer`, `validate`, `lint`, `test`,
`app`, `notebook`, `ci`, `clean`.

## The idea worth stealing: split targets by what they can access

The pipeline reads a private document corpus that exists on one machine. Rather than let a reader
discover that by running something and watching it fail, the file says so at the top and names
exactly which half works:

> "Targets that read the PRIVATE source (data, report, viewer) only work where that source +
> src/scrub_rules.local.py exist. On a clean clone, data/ and docs/ are already the safe output; use
> `db`, `docs`, `validate`, `test`, `app`, `notebook`."
> — labour-fraud-analysis-a-forensic-data-investigation/Makefile, 2026-07-11

Then the split is **encoded as a target**, not just documented:

> "ci: db docs validate lint test ## what CI runs on a clean clone (no private source)"
> — labour-fraud-analysis-a-forensic-data-investigation/Makefile, 2026-07-11

`make ci` is the clean-clone contract. Anyone can run it, and it is the same list
[[github-actions]] executes, so a green local run means something. `make all` is the private
superset. The Makefile is the one place where the boundary between "reproducible by anyone" and
"reproducible by one person" is written down — see [[reproducible-analysis]].

## Self-documenting help

```make
help:
	@grep -E '^[a-z].*:.*##' $(MAKEFILE_LIST) | sed 's/:.*## /\t/' | sort
```

Every target carries a `##` comment; `make help` greps them out of the file itself. The
documentation cannot drift from the target list because it *is* the target list — the same instinct
as [[generated-docs-checked-by-ci-diff]], applied to the build file. Compare
[[documentation-drift]], which is what happens everywhere this trick is not used.

## Overridable variables, not hard-coded paths

`PY ?= python`, plus `SOURCE ?=`, `REPORT ?=` and `VIEWER ?=` defaulting to sibling-directory paths
outside the repo. `?=` means an environment variable wins, so the private source can live anywhere
without editing the file — and no absolute path is committed.

## Targets that assert rather than build

Several targets exist to make a check runnable by name, which is what turns a claim into a command:

- `db` — "load data/csv -> data/data.sqlite (asserts 0 FK violations)"
- `validate` — "the leak-gate — must print RESULT: PASS", the [[disclosure-gate]]
- `docs` — regenerates the artefacts CI then diffs

That is [[verify-the-load-dont-declare-it]] wired into the entry point. `clean` removes only the
regenerated database, never `data/csv` — the published dataset is an input to the clean-clone path,
not an output of it.
